label: Zebda
note: Churned from raw milk that sours on its own, not from separated cream

about.text: The raw fresh butter of Morocco (zebda beldiya), churned from rayeb, raw milk left to sour for one to three days in an earthen jar or goatskin bag; the liquid left behind is lben. Salted and fermented, it becomes smen.

links.name: Benkirane et al., J. Microbiology, Biotechnology and Food Sciences (2022)

how.label: sour, churn
how.text: Raw milk is left to sour on its own until it clots; lactococci and leuconostocs make the acid and aroma, and churning the soured milk separates zebda beldia from the skimmed lben.

links.name: Ouadghiri et al. 2009, J Appl Microbiol (LAB in Moroccan lben)

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: At room temperature until it coagulates, the lben ending at a mean pH of 4.38 and 73–112 °D.
Yields zebda beldia (raw butter) and lben.
